 WhatsApp Android users may soon read messages without opening chats
 Published
 18 hours ago on
 November 5, 2026 
 By
 Sheetal Malviya 
 Share 
 Tweet 
 WhatsApp is preparing a new feature for Android users that will let them read messages without opening a chat. This feature will make it easier to check new messages and manage conversations directly from the chat list.
 With this feature, users will be able to tap and hold a chat to see a preview of the latest messages. They will not need to open the conversation to read them. The Android version will also allow users to scroll through the preview and read more messages.
 Along with the message preview, WhatsApp will show a menu with different options. Users will be able to mark a chat as read, pin it, archive it, select it, or delete it. By tapping “More options”, they will also be able to lock a chat, add it to a list, view chat information, and add the chat to their phone’s home screen.
 Image via WABetaInfo
 The most useful part of this feature is that users will be able to read new messages without marking the chat as read. This means they can check messages without updating read receipts. The chat will only be marked as read when they open the conversation normally.
 WhatsApp is still working on this feature, and it is not available to beta testers or regular users yet. The company has not shared an official release date.
 The feature has been spotted in the WhatsApp beta for Android 2.26.44.11 update, available on the Google Play Store. It is expected to arrive in a future WhatsApp Android update for everyone.

 India clears Samsung’s flagship Galaxy S27 for launch
 Published
 5 hours ago on
 November 5, 2026 
 By
 Yash Rathore 
 Samsung’s next-generation flagship phone has crossed a crucial regulatory milestone. The Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) has officially granted approval for the Galaxy S27, bearing the model number SM-S952B/DS, in India.
 The certification (spotted by AndroidTreasure ) marks the first formal regulatory clearance for the entry-tier Galaxy S27 line within the region, signaling that supply chain validation is advancing ahead of early 2027 market availability.
 While BIS documentation rarely publishes granular hardware metrics, the listing confirms dual-SIM capabilities for the regional variant and establishes a timeline consistent with Samsung’s historical release cycles.
 The regulatory paper trail provides critical context when cross-referenced with recent international database entries. Documentation filed with NBD previously tied the SM-S952B identification to a 6.3-inch display footprint.
 Crucially, those filings indicated that Samsung intends to equip the standard model with its in-house Exynos 2700 processor, complemented by a baseline configuration of 12GB of RAM and 256GB of internal storage.
 The choice of chip architecture suggests Samsung is maintaining its dual-sourcing strategy, reserving regional silicon for select Asian and European markets while maintaining alternative platform arrangements elsewhere. Advertisement 
 Certification disclosures from China’s 3C authority, coupled with safety filings at UL Solutions, confirm the SM-S952B supports 25W fast charging, prioritizing battery longevity and thermal mitigation over peak charging speeds.
 Early regulatory clearances of this nature typically precede mass assembly operations by approximately two to three months.
 By securing clearance from Indian regulators in early November, Samsung retains full operational flexibility to meet global logistics timelines, keeping its core product roadmap intact as component production scales up across partner facilities.

 Dylan Efron turns curiosity into creativity with Samsung Galaxy Tab S12 series campaign
 Published
 15 hours ago on
 November 5, 2026 
 By
 Sheetal Malviya 
 Samsung has launched a new campaign for its Galaxy Tab S12 Series, featuring TV star, producer, and outdoor enthusiast Dylan Efron. The campaign shows how the latest Galaxy tablets can help people learn new skills, explore their interests, and turn ideas into reality.
 The campaign features Efron in three videos, where he tries different activities with the help of experts. In the first video, he learns to design a surfboard at Rockaway Beach using the S Pen.
 In the second, he explores urban beekeeping with the help of Google Gemini. In the third video, he records sounds from a forest and uses the Galaxy Tab S12+ to create music. Through these activities, Samsung shows how its tablets can support learning, creativity, and new experiences.
 Talking about the campaign, Efron said he enjoys learning new things and trying activities he has never done before. He added that Galaxy technology inspires people to learn, grow, and explore their interests.
 The Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra and Galaxy Tab S12+ come with slim and durable designs, long-lasting battery life, and IP68 dust and water resistance. Both tablets include an S Pen for drawing, writing notes, and saving ideas. They also feature Dynamic AMOLED 2X displays for bright and clear visuals. Advertisement 
 Users can also enjoy Galaxy AI features and Google Gemini to find information, explore new topics, and work on creative projects. With this campaign, Samsung aims to show how the Galaxy Tab S12 Series can be a useful companion for people who love learning, creating, and trying new things. All three campaign videos are now available on YouTube.

 Samsung study reveals parents are turning to AI to decode new career options
 Published
 19 hours ago on
 November 5, 2026 
 By
 Sheetal Malviya 
 Samsung has revealed that around 73% of UK parents use search engines or AI chatbots to understand new qualifications and job roles before discussing them with their teenage children.
 The research shows that many parents struggle to guide their children about future careers because technology and job opportunities are changing quickly. Around 35% of parents say they cannot help their children understand today’s job market, while 40% are not confident about giving career advice. Also, 63% believe their teenagers know more about modern technology and future jobs than they do.
 Many parents are also unfamiliar with new education options. Around 45% do not know much about T-Levels, while 44% have little knowledge of Higher Technical Qualifications. More than half also find it difficult to explain new jobs such as AI Prompt Engineer and Climate Tech Specialist.
 To help young people explore future career options, Samsung has launched its seventh annual Samsung Solve for Tomorrow competition. It is open to students aged 11 to 18 across the UK and Ireland.
 TV presenter Joe Swash has also joined the campaign by visiting his local community to ask people about future careers. He found that many people were just as confused as parents.
 Students can take part alone or in teams of up to four. They must use technology to solve real-world problems under three themes: Smarter Sport, Greener Future and Safer Online. Advertisement 
 Entries are open until 18 January 2027. Selected students will receive mentoring and funding to develop their ideas. Finalists will also get work experience with Samsung, while winners will have their ideas displayed at Piccadilly Circus. The programme aims to help young people build skills, gain confidence and prepare for future careers.

 Samsung One UI 9.5 to bring new WeChat backup feature to Galaxy phones
 Published
 21 hours ago on
 November 5, 2026 
 By
 Sheetal Malviya 
 Samsung is working on making chat backups easier for Galaxy users with a new cloud backup feature for WeChat. Currently available on the Samsung W27 , the feature allows users to save their chats, voice messages, emojis, and shared files online. Samsung is also planning to bring this feature to more Galaxy devices with the One UI 9.5 update.
 The new service comes through a partnership between Samsung and Baidu Cloud. It allows users to back up their WeChat conversations to Baidu Netdisk, removing the need for manual backups. This can be helpful when switching to a new phone or recovering data after losing or damaging a device.
 Users can find the new option under Settings > Accounts and Backup. From there, they can create backups, download existing backups and restore their chat history whenever needed.
 Image via Samsung Members app
 Samsung says the backed-up data is encrypted during transfer and storage to keep users’ information safe. However, users need to install Baidu Netdisk and sign in to their Baidu account to use this service.
 Samsung has confirmed that the feature will also support Galaxy devices eligible for the One UI 9.5 update. However, the company has not shared a list of supported models yet. For now, Galaxy users will have to wait for more details about supported devices and availability.

 Samsung wins global DRAM crown in Q3, but surging SK Hynix narrows the gap
 Published
 1 day ago on
 November 5, 2026 
 By
 Yash Rathore 
 Samsung Electronics strengthened its presence in the global DRAM market, with its shipment share hitting a record 38 percent in Q3 2026. The company has not just retained its DRAM crown, but has widened the gap with SK Hynix.
 On November 5,  Counterpoint Research published fresh data on the worldwide DRAM market share in the third quarter. Samsung led the global DRAM market, followed by SK Hynix, Micron and CXMT in Q3 2026.
 Researchers at Counterpoint state that every new HBM generation is resetting the leadership position. For example, SK Hynix led with HBM3E , and Samsung snatched the crown with the rapid introduction of HBM4 semiconductor.
 “Every new HBM generation is resetting the leadership position,” said MS Hwang, Research Director at Counterpoint Research.
 HBM prices, which rose less than conventional DRAM earlier this year, are now catching up. Long-term agreements are underpinning prices, and with major new fabs not starting operations until 2028, the supply shortage will persist.
 In the third quarter of the year, Samsung’s DRAM share was 38 percent, much higher than 29 percent of SK Hynix. Micron and CXMT held third and fourth ranks with 21 percent and 9 percent market share, respectively. Advertisement 
 Global DRAM market chart in Q3 2026 :
 Samsung: 38%
 SK Hynix: 29%
 Micron: 21%
 CXMT: 9%
 China’s CXMT went aggressive with DRAM architecture, threatening global memory leaders. The company is also trying to enter the HBM market, but it’s not happening anytime soon, and that letdown is keeping its share restricted.
 Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix revealed long-term memory supply contracts during their Q3 2026 earnings call. Samsung, in particular, revealed ten LTAs along with ten more in talks with “good” progress.
